newsitem.title: SOMALIA: 30 reported killed in Somalia faction fighting.
newsitem.headline: 30 reported killed in Somalia faction fighting.

text.p: Some 30 militiamen were killed in fighting between rival forces in the Bakol region of southwest Somalia, radio reports from the area said on Friday.
Residents of Bakol said in radio contact with Mogadishu the fighting pitted militiamen loyal to south Mogadishu leader Hussein Aideed against the rebel Rahanwein Resistance Army (RRA) on Thursday.

The reports, which could not be independently verified, said Aideed's men were ambushed as they left nine "technical" battlewagons to search for RRA fighters in Dhiil village, 32 km (20 miles) north of Huddor town.
The reports spoke of at least 12 wounded in the clashes.
Radio North Mogadishu, opposed to Aideed, quoted an RRA spokesman as saying four technicals were destroyed and arms were seized in the fighting. He said all the dead were Aideed's militiamen.
No spokesman for Aideed was available to comment on the report.
The RRA has mounted intermittent hit-and-run attacks against Aideed's forces since they seized the southern town of Baidoa in September 1995.

Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991. Aideed was elected president by supporters last year but rival faction leaders have rejected the move and his administration.
